faults.fault: When the prop is widened the backbox widens with it: the backglass artwork stretches, the score displays are doubled/streaked ('00' becomes garbled columns), the artwork becomes mirrored blobs, and the speaker grilles triplicate. The backbox must stay a single cabinet width holding ONE playfield's artwork — the widened backbox reads as a smeared second game. Blocking.
Vertical streak/banding artifacts on the cabinet body and leg textures where the prop was enlarged — visible smear trails a player could point at. Blocking.

wider_means: A wider pinball is a broader cabinet body and backbox spanning the same single playfield -- wider side rails and a wider coin-door panel, never a second game.
taller_means: A taller pinball is one with longer legs and a longer plain cabinet run under the playfield; the backbox and glass stay the same size, so the extra height goes into the cabinet body and legs, not a taller backbox or taller artwork.

A wider pinball must keep ONE backbox layout — one title, one pair of speakers, two score windows — with plain extension at the ends, not repeats. A wider pinball is a broader cabinet spanning one playfield with wider side rails and the SAME single coin door and button pair; the extra fittings read as a repeat artifact, not a decision.

In the tallered version (image 4) the extra height partly went into the backbox — the marquee text and score windows render larger/stretched rather than staying fixed size, contrary to the rule that taller means longer legs and a longer cabinet run while the backbox stays the same.
